result.note: Tests the US waiver for Russian crude and India's Hormuz exposure and reserve cover, plus Hormuz's share of world oil trade; Moscow's offer is skipped as an unconfirmed proposal.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's crude oil supply as reported in March 2026:
items: The US Treasury granted India a 30-day waiver to buy Russian crude already loaded on tankers.
Around 40% of India's crude imports pass through the Strait of Hormuz.
India's strategic reserves cover about 60 days of crude supply.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: India's strategic reserves cover only 20-25 days of crude supply, not 60 days, so statement 3 is wrong. The US Treasury granted the 30-day waiver on 6 March 2026, as the Middle East conflict disrupted shipping through Hormuz, even though India had earlier reduced Russian oil purchases under US pressure.
questions.source: Around 40% of India’s crude imports pass through Hormuz, while strategic reserves cover only 20-25 days of crude supply

questions.prompt: In March 2026, shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was disrupted by conflict in the Middle East. Roughly what share of the world's oil trade does the strait normally carry?
questions.explain: Hormuz normally carries about one-fifth of the world's oil trade, so even partial disruption pushes prices higher. In March 2026, insurers pulled war-risk coverage and shipping companies suspended Gulf transits.
questions.source: Hormuz normally carries about 1/5 of the world’s oil trade, so even partial disruption sends prices higher.
